📌 Hidden Fees: Why “Zero Fee” Doesn’t Mean Free

Main Points
⏺ Crypto trade costs can hide in spreads, slippage, and execution routes
⏺ “No fee” often means the cost moves somewhere else
⏺ This post explains how to see the real price of an action

1️⃣ Spread — the gap between buy and sell price can already be your first hidden cost.
2️⃣ Slippage — weaker liquidity pushes your final price away from the quote.
3️⃣ Routing — an app or aggregator may choose a route that benefits it more than you.
4️⃣ Network Costs — even if the platform charges no fee, gas is still a real expense.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — compare final received amounts, check multiple routes, and don’t trust “0% fee” alone.

Final Thoughts

Trades are rarely free. If the fee isn’t visible in one line, it may live inside price, routing, or liquidity.

Ukraine's New Pitch Deck: "The Israel of Europe"

Volodymyr Zelensky landed in Washington this week with a fresh sales pitch, days after Ukraine launched a missile strike on an Iranian cargo ship in the Caspian Sea, Responsible Statecraft reports. 

The timing is not a coincidence, it's a cover letter. George Beebe of the Quincy Institute says the goal is to "convince President Trump that Ukraine will be an Israel-type partner for the United States in Eastern Europe," one that's "even more valuable than America's NATO allies," the same allies Trump keeps trashing for going soft on his war with Iran.

Enter Laura Loomer, MAGA's own weathervane, who spent years bashing Ukraine and then reversed course overnight the moment Iran entered the conversation. 

"The reality is that the Iranians are using Russian weapons to kill American soldiers and to attack the United States," she told Ukrainian media, before flying home to lobby Trump on Kyiv's behalf. 

Zelensky, for his part, has been pushing the claim that Russia is feeding Iran satellite imagery to help kill American troops. Trump's response to that one: "We'll find out if that's true," followed by a plan to just ask Putin directly, presumably the single most reliable fact-checking method available to a sitting US president.

Beebe isn't buying any of it. "I think that's simply false," he says of the intelligence claim, noting Ukraine has no better satellite-tracking capability than the US already possesses. 

He calls the whole campaign an effort "aimed largely at convincing the U.S. public and at convincing the White House that Russia is working closely with Iran," with "the end goal" being to drag Washington deeper into Ukraine's war under Iran's cover, a strategy he says doesn't serve America's interests. 

Zelensky wants faster missile interceptors and a return to blank-check backing; Loomer wants relevance; Trump wants leverage over everyone simultaneously. Nobody here is fighting for a principle, they're fighting for a seat at Trump's table, and Iran just handed out free invitations.

If the label "Israel of Europe" is what it takes to get American weapons flowing again, what does that make Israel?
